reason: While the Assyrian elite (Sennacherib and his officials Rab-shakeh) are indeed portrayed unfavorably as arrogant, blasphemous, and ultimately defeated, other elite figures in the text are portrayed favorably or with respect. Hezekiah, the Judahite king, ultimately shows faith and is vindicated by divine protection. The Judahite officials (Eliakim, Shebna, Joah) are portrayed as wise and respectful. Most significantly, Isaiah the prophet—part of the religious elite—is portrayed very positively as a conduit of divine wisdom and encouragement. The text does not uniformly portray 'people from the elite' unfavorably; rather, it contrasts the arrogant foreign elite with faithful and wise leaders of Judah.
